To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
happiness is associated with left frontal activation and disgust is associated with right frontal activation.

1) happiness and disgust are associated with different patterns of frontal and anterior temporal brain activation; 2) these patterns correspond to the facial expressions of happiness and disgust, respectively; and 3) the patterns are consistent with the approach and withdrawal nature of these emotions, and with the notion that the left and right hemispheres are specialized for the processing of information related to approach and withdrawal, respectively
1. The left hemisphere is more active than the right hemisphere during positive emotion, and the right hemisphere is more active during negative emotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of emotional experience and the role of approach/withdrawal motivation in emotional responding.
the relationship between brain and behavior, and with the nature of the brain mechanisms that mediate emotional expression.
the relationship between emotion and brain asymmetry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

happiness is associated with left sided anterior asymmetry, disgust is associated with right sided anterior asymmetry; and that happiness and disgust, but not other emotions, are associated with anterior asymmetry.
happiness is associated with left sided anterior brain activity whereas disgust is associated with right sided anterior brain activity.
the right hemisphere has a special role in processing negative emotions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the right frontal region may be a neural substrate for emotional approach, and that the left frontal region may be important for emotional withdrawal.
the right frontal region is involved in the processing of negative emotion and the left frontal region is involved more in the processing of positive emotion.
the left hemisphere is associated with the experience of positive emotions and approach motivation, and the right hemisphere is associated with negative emotions and withdrawal motivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the left frontal region of the brain is associated with approach-related behavior, while the right is associated with withdrawal.
we can use the brain to understand the emotions that people experience.
we can measure brain asymmetries associated with emotional expression, and these asymmetries are consistent across individuals and across different emotions.
